1.5 CONSTRUCTION PROCEDURES
Construction of the project would require relocation of a 0.4 mile segment of South Carolina Route 171. The segment would be relocated to the west side of the upper reservoir west dam. The Applicant's construction schedule is shown in Figure 1-10.
Improvements to the existing road to the pilot tunnel portal area were to have begun in August 1976, and the excavation of the pilot tunnel and exploratory borings therein commenced in October 1976. Construction of permanent access road is scheduled to start in October 1977.
In 1978, a steel cellular cofferdam would be built around the lower outlet structure area in the Jocassee Reservoir. Excavation of the upper intake channel, ventilation shaft, access tunnel portal, and tailrace channel would also begin along with the installation of construction plant.
In 1979, the main underground excavation for the power tunnel, tailrace tunnels, and powerhouse cavern would begin. Construction of the main dam would start in 1979.
In 1980, the major excavation work would be completed and the work of concrete lining of the ventilation shaft, concrete work for the powerhouse, and installation of the steel lining of the penstock section would begin. The powerhouse cranes would be installed.
In 1981, the concrete work for the power tunnel and shaft and tailrace tunnels would be completed.
In 1982, the concrete work for the upper intake structure would be completed. Concrete work for the lower outlet structure, switchyard station, mechanical and electrical equipment installation, and installation of Unit No. 1 would begin.
In 1983, the construction of the main dam and the dikes would be completed. Cofferdams would be removed. Installation of Units Nos. 1 and 2 would be completed and the units placed in commercial operation. Installation of Unit No. 3 would begin.
